title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v10
content:
Purpose: quick back-of-envelope for pricing/packaging options (hosted + reserved/dedicated).

Assumptions (base):
- GPU infra blended cost: $1.80 / GPU-hour (after DC + infra + ops amortization).  Example baseline: p4d-ish fleet blended avg.
- Serving efficiency: 8k tokens generated per GPU-hour at typical batch sizes (this is variable by model + batching).
- Effective tokens per second (per GPU): ~2.22 t/s -> ~8k tokens/hour (sanity check).
- Other infra (control plane, storage, logging): add $0.20 / GPU-hour (blended) -> total infra $2.00 / GPU-hour.
- Average request composition: prompt_in = 40 tokens, gen_out = 80 tokens => total 120 tokens per call.
- Cache/batching savings: naive hosted avg token cost multiplier = 1.0; with batching/caching we might get 1.6x efficiency (i.e., 8k -> 12.8k tokens/hr).  Use hit rates 0%/20%/40% as scenarios.
- Model cost/royalty: assume open weights (no per-token model fee). If we supported third-party model licensing, add per-token fee later.

Unit math (baseline):
- Tokens per GPU-hour = 8,000 tokens (no batching).
- Cost per token = $2.00 / 8,000 = $0.00025 per token.
- With batching/caching (1.6x) tokens/hr = 12,800 -> cost per token = $2.00 / 12,800 = $0.00015625 per token.

Per-call economics (avg 120 tokens):
- Cost per call (no batching): 120 * $0.00025 = $0.03
- Cost per call (with batching): 120 * $0.00015625 = $0.01875

Margin targets: want gross margin >= 60% (for hosted API business). Therefore suggested retail multipliers: x2.5 - x4 on raw token cost depending on feature set and support.
- If raw cost per token = $0.00015625, retail target range = $0.00039 - $0.000625 per token.
- That implies per-call price (avg 120 tokens): $0.0468 - $0.075.

Tier sketch (hosted API):
- Free tier: 100k tokens / month free + throttled rate (to drive PLG).
- Developer: $20 / month -> 2M tokens (implied $0.00001 per token). This is subsidized to drive adoption; include rate limits and no SLA.
- Team: $250 / month -> 15M tokens + shared workspace + basic support. Effective unit price ~ $0.0000167/token. (We might be below cost for small customers; assume we expect active usage + paid seat revenue).
- Business: $2,500 / month -> 200M tokens + SSO + logs + 24h support. Effective unit price $0.0000125/token.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: Custom pricing. Usually based on reserved GPU-hours + overage token price + premium support.

Comments on above: Developer/Team numbers intentionally aggressive to foster adoption; loss leader. Need clear limits to avoid abuse (rate limits, prompt size caps, post-payment verification).

Dedicated / Reserved model (back-of-envelope):
- Offer reserved pools: customers commit to GPU-hours/month. Example unit: 1 reserved GPU = 720 GPU-hours/mo. Price options: discounted fully-managed price = cost * markup.
- If blended infra cost = $2.00 / GPU-hr, monthly infra cost per reserved GPU = 720 * $2.00 = $1,440.
- Add ops/managed service margin + hardware amortization + support: target price to customer ~$3,600 - $4,800 per GPU/mo (2.5x - 3.3x).
- Map to token capacity: at 8k tokens/hr -> 720 * 8k = 5.76M tokens/GPU/mo (no batching). With batching 1.6x -> ~9.216M tokens.
- Example offering: Reserved-1 (1 GPU) = $4,000/mo -> ~9.2M tokens -> effective token price $0.000434/token (includes SLA + isolation). Overages billed at a higher per-token rate or bursts on shared pool.

Overage pricing and mixed fleets:
- Overages should be expensive to encourage commitments: e.g., 2x - 3x the hosted per-token price.
- Support a fallback pool (cheaper model variants) for graceful degradation to keep apps online but at lower quality/cost.

Embedding pricing (notes):
- Embedding compute more expensive per token due to longer forward passes? Not necessarily; but embeddings are often priced per 1k vectors or per 1k tokens. We should adopt per-embedding unit price.
- Baseline: assume same token throughput as generation for simple models. Offer embedding-specific tiers: $0.01 / 1k embeddings for hosted (example).

Other levers to influence unit economics:
- Quantization & distillation: use 8-bit or 4-bit runtimes to increase tokens/hr -> lowers cost/token.
- KV/prefix caching: heavy reuse workloads can drop token compute by large factor.
- Batch size opt + dynamic batching: increases GPU utilization during spikes.
- Model routing: route to cheaper model variants for non-sensitive or lower-quality workloads.

Sample pricing experiments to run (A/B):
1) Per-token vs per-request pricing: keep both but favored per-token. Evaluate adoption friction.
2) Prepaid bundles: 1M token bundle at a marginally discounted price vs monthly subscription including burst.
3) Developer promotional pricing (first 6 months) with hard caps to avoid runaways.
4) Dedicated commit discounts: 1x/3x/12x term length discounts (monthly reduction with longer commitments).

Quick sensitivity checks:
- If tokens/hr improves from 8k -> 16k (quant + better batching), cost/token halves. With retail multiplier 3x, price/token still competitive.
- If average call grows from 120 -> 300 tokens (complex prompts), per-call cost increases from $0.01875 -> $0.0469 (with batching). Need to surface prompt size to customers (quota by tokens).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate actual tokens/hr for our verified model fleet across typical workloads (chat vs completion vs embeddings).
- Get more precise infra blended cost (region differences, spot vs on-demand, egress, storage).
- Consider differential pricing for streaming vs non-streaming (latency premium?).
- Decide how to price function-calls / tool invocation complexity (maybe treat as normal tokens but consider extra fixed per-call overhead).
- Investigate competitor public prices and market anchors (OpenAI, Cohere, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock).

Notes to self: keep this doc rough. Convert to a cleaner PRD when we have real telemetry: tokens/hr by model, actual infra $/hr, cache-hit distributions, and customer usage histograms.

End.
